event_description: State disaster declaration for Ford, Greene, Logan, Morgan, Randolph, Sangamon and Scott counties after the March 11 to 12, 2006 storms and tornadoes.
State disaster declaration for the November 30 to December 1, 2006 ice storm, issued December 5, 2006 (Governor's release of January 29, 2007).

State disaster declaration for Cook, DeKalb, DuPage, Grundy, Kane, Lake, LaSalle, McHenry and Will counties for the late August 2007 flooding and storms, declared quickly after the storms (dated release of September 14, 2007).
Cook County declared an emergency area on September 14, 2008 for the weekend flooding, widened on September 16 to Cook and six other counties as state disaster areas.

State disaster declaration for Alexander, Hardin, Johnson, Massac, Pope, Pulaski and Union counties for the January 2009 ice storm, issued January 30, 2009 (Illinois delegation release of February 13, 2009).
State disaster declaration for three Southern Illinois counties after the May 8, 2009 storms (dated statement of May 9, 2009).
State disaster declaration for 12 counties after the July 23 to 24, 2010 thunderstorms and flooding.
Statewide disaster declaration issued ahead of the February 1 to 2, 2011 blizzard.
Disaster proclamation for southern Illinois after two weeks of severe storms and flooding.
State disaster proclamation for 38 counties after heavy rain caused flash flooding and record river flooding (later expanded to 44 counties).
Gubernatorial disaster proclamation for Champaign, Grundy, LaSalle, Massac, Tazewell, Washington and Woodford counties after severe storms with tornadoes and straight-line winds.
State disaster proclamation for 23 counties after June and July storms with heavy rainfall, flash and river flooding, tornadoes and straight-line winds.
State disaster proclamation for Calhoun, Jackson, Jersey, Madison, Monroe, Randolph and St. Clair counties for flooding.
State disaster proclamation for Kane, McHenry and Lake counties (Cook County added July 16) for flooding on the Des Plaines and Fox rivers after heavy rainfall.
State disaster proclamation for flooding in 34 counties along the Mississippi and Illinois rivers after heavy rainfall (renewed May 31, June 28 and July 29, 2019).
State disaster proclamation for 28 counties after tornadoes and high winds on December 10, 2021, including the Edwardsville warehouse collapse in Madison County.
State disaster proclamation for St. Clair and Washington counties after severe weather, torrential rain and flash flooding on July 25 and 27, 2022.
Disaster proclamation for Cook, Henry, Fulton, St. Clair, Washington, Winnebago and Will counties for the July 13 to 16, 2024 severe storms, tornadoes and flooding.
